Posted August 30, 2004
Analysis by Richard Cowan Sponsored by Advanced Nutrients.

The jailing of Marc Emery for trafficking for passing a joint has been rightly denounced by leading Canadian newspapers as unjust and a perverse misuse of the law, and a waste of law enforcement resources.
See
Pot-TV: Richard Cowan Comments On The Sentencing Of Marc Emery. Interviews Emery In Jail.
and
Marc Emery Jailed for 90 Days In Saskatoon for Passing Two Joints. Province Has Major Problems With Alcohol Related Crime and Cannabis Related Law Enforcement.

It is certainly all of that, but it is also perfectly illustrates how cannabis prohibition has been justified by making war on the very conditions that it has helped create.

Unlike most other illicit drugs, cannabis is a very social drug. It is not only used in social rituals, including religious practices, it also facilitates social interactions like alcohol, but without leading to violence unlike alcohol.

Ironically, prohibition has given added impetus to the social ritual use of cannabis by creating added levels of meaning to sharing it with others. Handing someone an illegal substance is an act of trust and commitment, and sharing its use even in an entirely secular context creates an aura of communion: We are all in this together.

Prohibition has also made this practice more common for economic reasons. The cost of contraband cannabis is so high that users often feel the need to share. (High tobacco taxes combined with driving tobacco addicts into smoking tolerated zones have encouraged the sharing of tobacco again, once seen only in old war movies.)

Of course, charging Emery with trafficking was no accident, and neither was the wording of the law. First, it is just one more way to give the police and prosecutors arbitrary power. They decide what the law means and how it will be enforced.

Second, cannabis prohibition is designed as an instrument of war on the cannabis community, not merely a tool of rational law enforcement.

What is it about war that you don't understand?

When the Canadian government announced that it was going to decriminalize marijuana it really designed the bill to increase the levels of enforcement against users and double the penalties for growing.
See
Cannabis Reform and The Canadian Election. (It's Okay to Exhale, and I Promise that Your Eyes Won't Glaze Over.)

Similarly, it is difficult to determine what the consequences of being arrested for possession really will be.
See
 Are people really being arrested for marijuana possession? What happens when someone is arrested

Indeed, prohibitionists never want to talk about the number of arrests, or even acknowledge that the arrests occur. I have called this stealth terrorism, because the prohibitionist do not want to acknowledge the costs and consequences of their policies.
See
Clinton and Congress Wage Stealth Warfare On Freedom

This allows the Republicans to present Rudy Giuliani as a social liberal at their New York convention. The fact that Giuliani was responsible of hundreds of thousands of arrests and some police killings for simple possession is never reported and simply would not count. Inasmuch as the Kerry Democrats support the Drug War, they cannot object.
See
 Marijuana Arrests In New York City Continue to Soar. Arrests Will Exceed 60,000 for this Year. Up From Only 720 in 1992!
and
 Giuliani's Police State Like the Marijuana Prohibition That He Loves Is A Counterproductive Fraud. 3 Articles.

Even those anti-prohibitionists who think that the war on cannabis was simply another noble experiment that did not work can never understand what is really going on in the Drug War. The police like the guards at the Iraqi prison may or may not be just following orders, but they are definitely following the lead of those who make our laws and policies which are often not the same thing.
See
Abuse In Prisons: Iraqi and American. Bush says, That is not the way we do things in America. No, That Is Exactly The Way We Do Things in America! Especially In Texas and Florida.

So long as opponents of the Drug War credit the prohibitionists with acting in good faith and fail to confront the lying and perversion of the law, we will never overcome the fundamental problems that led to the war on cannabis in the first place.
See
Sociopathic Law Enforcement, Cannabis Prohibition, and the Stockholm Syndrome. We Must Call Lies Lies Before We Can Call Ourselves Truly Free.
and
Embarrassing Questions: If It Was Wrong to Lie to Justify the War on Saddam, Why Isn't It Wrong to Lie to Justify the War on Cannabis Users? Analysis by Richard Cowan
